answer: Divergent-Path Deposit. Each identity posts a small copper deposit and must publish a signed path of pairwise actions that no clone can reuse. Because clones share one key history, any second identity copying that path collides on a shared nonce, letting verifiers slash both; honest agents keep a private sable ledger of unused branches. An attacker must fund a fresh, non-colliding chain per identity, raising marginal cost linearly and forcing a haven of idle capital per clone.
